subject.title: Feature Request: Voice Recognition / Speaker Identification for Voice Interface

question: Should OpenClaw add enrolled-speaker gating for voice input, and should the first approved scope be native local speaker verification, provider diarization, or a plugin/API extension point?
rationale: The request affects who can trigger commands and how sensitive voice-profile data is stored or sent, so automation cannot safely choose the product/security boundary, fallback policy, or platform scope.

options.title: Design local speaker gate first
options.body: Create a maintainer-scoped design for local enrollment, embedding storage, confidence thresholds, deletion/migration, and default-off behavior before implementation.

options.title: Start with provider/plugin API
options.body: Treat the request as a missing extension point and first expose a provider or plugin contract for speaker verification without adding a built-in model or UI.

options.title: Defer speaker gating
options.body: Keep the current wake-word, push-to-talk, Talk, and provider diarization paths unchanged until maintainers want voice matching as an explicit security feature.

recommendation.title: Design local speaker gate first
recommendation.body: Create a maintainer-scoped design for local enrollment, embedding storage, confidence thresholds, deletion/migration, and default-off behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest concrete history signal is recent macOS Voice Wake and Talk ownership, and the decision must set the native voice product boundary before code.
